claim: Return on attack (RoA) is an attacker-side efficiency metric, with Cremonini and Martini as a source.
quote: We have called it Return-On-Attack (ROA) and it is de ned as the gain the attacker expects from a successful attack over the losses that he sustains due to the adoption of security measure S by his target.
locator: Sec. 2, PDF p. 2 (workshop paper; no printed page numbers, WEIS 2005 published no proceedings)
issue: Survives the adversarial read: ROA is the attacker's expected gain over its cost, an attacker-side efficiency measure. Caveats, none changing the cell: the source is not about MTD (alavizadeh2022 carries the MTD use), it says ROA is 'the evaluation an organization does' of an attacker's convenience, and it writes 'ROA', not 'RoA'.
